articles.title: 1 Month of Discord Nitro for GOG Customers and GOG Galaxy Users
articles.body:
Starting from October 28th, 2026 (3PM CET) to November 5th, 2026 (9AM CET), eligible GOG customers and GOG Galaxy users can claim 1 month of Discord Nitro. Learn below about how you can claim Discord Nitro. 

Promotion Summary

Offer Details: 1 month of Discord Nitro

Who is Eligible to Redeem: Users who have had an active Nitro subscription or Nitro trial in the last 12 months are not eligible to redeem this Nitro promotion.

Note: This promotion is not eligible in the following regions: Syria, Ukraine, Russia, Iran, Turkey, and North Korea.

We may add additional restrictions from time to time, if you receive an "Unknown Gift Code" error during the claim/redemption process, you are not eligible to redeem this promotion. You can learn more at this Help Center article.

Users who have had a Discord Nitro subscription at any point on their accounts and have had a Nitro Classic or Nitro Basic subscription in the past 12 months are ineligible to redeem this promotion.

If a user has had a Nitro Basic, Nitro Classic, or Server Boosting subscription active on their account and they've never had a Nitro subscription, redeeming this promotion will override that subscription.

We will not be able to refund any leftover subscription time from those, and the user will be forfeiting the remainder of the existing subscription when activating the 1 month Nitro trial.

Users who have already claimed a gift from this promotion are not eligible to claim further gifts from this promotion.

This promotion is not eligible in the following regions: Syria, Ukraine, Russia, Iran, and North Korea. If you receive an "Unknown Gift Code" error during the claim/redemption process, you are not eligible to redeem this promotion. You can learn more at this Help Center article.

Requirements: Purchase one or more games during GOG’s 18th Anniversary Sale, running from October 28th, 2026 (3PM CET) to November 5th, 2026 (9AM CET), for a final gross amount of at least $10 (or local equivalent) paid at the checkout and have marketing consent for the email address tied to your GOG account. Eligible users will receive an email with a link to redeem the Nitro promotion. You must redeem the promotion in your Discord account by December 5th, 2026 (9AM CET).

Subscription: After the 1 month trial period, your Nitro subscription will convert to a monthly recurring subscription, and Discord will bill your payment method per month until you cancel it. You can cancel at any time in your Discord User Settings.

What this article covers:

  • Promotion Summary
  • What is Discord Nitro?
  • What is GOG?
  • How do I claim the Nitro Promo from my GOG account?
  • How do I redeem the Nitro Trial on my Discord Account?
    • Eligibility for Redeeming the Nitro Trial
    • Step by Step Redeem Instructions
    • What if I am an Active Nitro Basic, Nitro Classic, or Server Boosting Subscriber?
  • How do I share my Code with a Friend?
  • Frequently Asked Questions
    • Promotion Details
    • Eligibility for the Promotion
    • Payment Info and Subscription Questions
    • Potential Errors and Other Issues

What is Discord Nitro?

Discord Nitro is our Subscription plan that gives you access to special perks that'll make your time on Discord as fun as ever! Personalize and enhance your experience with popular perks like HD streaming, 500MB file uploads, profile and avatar customizations, 2 free Server Boosts, and more:

  • Custom Emojis
  • Discord App Color Themes
  • Super Reactions
  • Avatar Decorations
  • Unique Server Profiles
  • Server Boosts
  • More Nitro & Nitro Basic perks

What is GOG?

Founded in 2008, GOG is a leading European platform for digital game distribution that lets you legally and safely buy, download, and play the best editions of classic games, as well as newer releases and indies. Its mission is to Make Games Live Forever, which includes ensuring iconic games remain compatible with modern systems and supporting game preservation efforts.

GOG Galaxy is GOG's optional desktop client that brings modern features like automatic updates, cloud saves, multiplayer integration, and a universal game library, allowing you to connect and manage games from multiple platforms in one place.

How do I claim the Nitro Promo from my GOG account?

1) Check your email (with marketing consent) tied to your GOG account

If you made a qualifying purchase and have marketing consent, start by logging into the email that is tied to your GOG account, and then check your inbox for a new email from the GOG team.

You can also search for "Nitro" in your email inbox.

2) Press on the Nitro promotion link

Once you have found the email, press on the button or promotion link within the email and you'll be automatically redirected to a browser window to redeem the promotion.

The unique promotion link will look like this: https://discord.com/billing/promotions/XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX

How do I redeem the Nitro Trial on my Discord Account?

Once you have claimed the promo link, you'll now need to officially redeem this promo link on your Discord account (or share this code with a friend). You must redeem this Nitro trial by December 5, 2026 (9AM CET), i.e. thirty (30) days after the Promotion Period ends on November 5th, 2026 (9AM CET).

Eligibility for Redeeming the Nitro Trial

Note: This promotion is not eligible in the following regions: Syria, Ukraine, Russia, Iran, and North Korea.

We may add additional restrictions from time to time, if you receive an "Unknown Gift Code" error during the claim/redemption process, you are not eligible to redeem this promotion. You can learn more at this Help Center article.

Users who have had an active Nitro subscription or Nitro trial in the last 12 months are not eligible to redeem this Nitro promotion.

Users who have had a Discord Nitro subscription at any point on their accounts and have had a Nitro Classic or Nitro Basic subscription in the past 12 months are ineligible to redeem this promotion.

If a user has had a Nitro Basic, Nitro Classic, or Server Boosting subscription active on their account and they've never had a Nitro subscription, redeeming this promotion will override that subscription.

Users who have already claimed a gift from this promotion are not eligible to claim further gifts from this promotion.

Step by Step Redeem Instructions

If you're eligible and ready to redeem this Nitro subscription on your own Discord account, you can follow these steps below to redeem the promo.

Note:

  • Before redeeming Nitro, make sure you are logged in your own Discord account.
  • If you accidentally redeemed the Nitro promo on an account that is not yours, we are unable to provide you with another promo.

Step 1 - Pressing the Promo Link/Copying and Pasting into your Browser Window

Start by directly pressing the promotion link or copying and pasting the promotion link into your browser window.

Note: If you're redeeming this Nitro promo link in the Discord Gift Inventory, enter only your unique 24-digit code from the Nitro promotion link in the following format: XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX

Step 2 - Logging into Discord

If you're not already logged into Discord in your browser, you will then be automatically redirected to either:

Create an account Page (Left) and Login Page (Right)

Step 3 - Confirming the Correct Account and Payment Method

Once you have logged into your Discord account, you'll see a new message asking you to confirm that you are accepting the Nitro subscription on the correct Discord account.

You'll see a notice saying: "You are accepting this gift as _________"

If your Discord account does not have your payment information, you'll be asked to fill out your payment details. (Note: You will not be charged until the free trial ends and the subscription renews)

When you've filled out all the necessary information and you're ready to redeem this promotion, press the "Accept Gift" button.

Note: If you're logged into the incorrect Discord account, press the "Wrong account" button to login to the other account.

Step 4 - Subscription Now Activated

After accepting the promo to your account, you'll now be automatically redirected to your Subscriptions tab in your User Settings to see your newly activated Nitro subscription on your account.

What if I am an Active Nitro Basic, Nitro Classic, or Server Boosting Subscriber?

Just to clarify - if you have had a Discord Nitro subscription at any point on your account and have had a Nitro Classic or Nitro Basic subscription in the past 12 months, you are ineligible to redeem this promotion.

So long as you have had a Nitro Basic, Nitro Classic, or Server Boosting subscription active on your account and you've never had a Nitro subscription, you will be able to redeem this promotion and replace it with the 1 month Nitro subscription.

Important: By choosing to activate this 1 month trial, you will lose any features associated with your current subscriptions, and you will not receive a refund for any remaining value on your current subscription.

At the end of your 1 month trial period, you'll be converted to a paying Nitro subscription per month unless you cancel your subscription.

How do I share my Code with a Friend?

If you're unable to redeem the Nitro subscription link, you can share this link with a friend to use instead.

After you press on and open the promotion link, you can directly copy the promotion URL link in the new page and send it to a friend. We recommend sending the link in a private direct message. Make sure your friend redeems the code by December 5, 2026 (9AM CET).

Frequently Asked Questions

We know there's a lot of information to unpack on this promotion above, so we've also broken down this information in this FAQ section as well too.

  • Promotion Details
  • Eligibility for the Promotion
  • Payment Info and Subscription Questions
  • Potential Errors and Other Issues

Promotion Details

Q: How long does this promotion run for?

A: Eligible GOG customers and GOG Galaxy users can claim Discord Nitro promo between October 28th, 2026 (3PM CET) and November 5th, 2026 (9AM CET).

After November 5th, 2026 (9AM CET), GOG customers and GOG Galaxy users will no longer be able to claim a trial promo.

Q: How long does the Discord Nitro promotion last for?

A: You must redeem the Nitro promotion by December 5th, 2026 (9AM CET).

If a code has not been redeemed to the Discord account by December 5th, 2026 (9AM CET), it will expire and you will no longer be able to have 1 month of Discord Nitro.

Eligibility for the Promotion

Q: Who can claim this promotion from their GOG account?

A: GOG users with marketing consent who purchase one or more games for a final gross amount of at least $10 (or local equivalent) paid at checkout during GOG’s 18th Anniversary Sale, running from October 28th, 2026 (3PM CET) to November 5th, 2026 (9AM CET).

Q: Who can redeem this Nitro trial to their Discord account?

A: Users who have never had an active Nitro subscription on their Discord accounts are eligible to redeem this Nitro promotion.

Additionally, users who previously had a Discord Nitro subscription and have had a Nitro Classic or Nitro Basic subscription in the past 12 months are ineligible.

This promotion is not available in the following regions: Syria, Ukraine, Russia, Iran, and North Korea. If you receive an "Unknown Gift Code" error during the claim/redemption process, you are not eligible to redeem this promotion. You can learn more at this Help Center article.

Q: What if I'm a current or previous Nitro Basic, Nitro Classic, or a Server Boost subscription? Can I also take part in this promotion?

A: If you previously had a Discord Nitro subscription at any point on your accounts and have had a Nitro Classic or Nitro Basic subscription in the past 12 months, you are ineligible to redeem this promotion.

If you have had a Nitro Basic, Nitro Classic, or Server Boosting subscription active on your account and you've never had a Nitro subscription, you will be able to redeem this promotion and replace it with the 1 month Nitro subscription.

Important: By choosing to activate this 1 month trial, you will lose any features associated with your current subscriptions, and you will not receive a refund for any remaining value on your current subscription.

At the end of the promotion period, you'll be converted to a paying Nitro subscription per month unless you cancel your subscription.

Payment Info and Subscription Questions

Q: Why do I need to submit my payment info to redeem Nitro?

A: Because Nitro is a subscription plan, at the end of your 1 month trial, we will start your first billing cycle so you can continue to enjoy Nitro on Discord.

However, you can cancel the Nitro subscription at any time before the end of the 1 month.

Q: Why do I see a temporary hold/charge on my account when this is supposed to be a free promotion?

A: Just to clarify, this Nitro promotion is free, however, there will be a temporary hold placed on the payment method upon activating the promotion. This is to help Discord confirm the payment method works as expected and to prevent the use of fraudulent payment methods. This charge will appear in your Discord transaction history, and it may appear as a hold on your payment method.

We immediately reverse the temporary hold, and you'll see that reflected in your Discord transaction history. Your bank may take longer to remove the hold from your payment method.

Note: Banks will usually remove the temporary hold from your account within a few business days.

If your Discord transaction history does not show the hold released after 5 business days, please let us know at https://dis.gd/contact, and our support team will be able to investigate this issue further.

Potential Errors and Other Issues

Q: What if I didn't receive an email from GOG with the Nitro promo link, even if I'm a GOG customer or GOG Galaxy user?

A: In order to receive an email from GOG with the Nitro promo link, you must be a GOG customer or GOG Galaxy user who has made a qualifying purchase during GOG’s 18th Anniversary Sale.

Additionally, make sure that you've opted to receive marketing emails from GOG. If you've unsubscribed, you sadly won't be able to see this offer.

If you believe you are eligible for the promotion, contact GOG's support team: https://support.gog.com/hc/en-us

Q: I see a Sad Trombone error when I try to redeem my Nitro promo link.

A: Would you happen to be entering this Nitro promo link from the promotion into the Discord Gift Inventory or as a link within Discord chat?

If so, this is the incorrect method for redeeming the Nitro promo link, and you will see an error when attempting to redeem the promotion.

In order to successfully claim this promotion, try opening up an incognito browser and then copy and pasting the promotion link into your browser's address bar (also known as a location bar or URL bar).

Alternatively, in the Discord Gift Inventory, enter only your unique 24-digit code from the Nitro promotion link in the following format: XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX

Q: I see a "Oh no! It looks like you have Nitro already" error when I try to redeem my Nitro promo link.

A: If you're seeing an "Oh no! It looks like you have Nitro already" error, that means that the Discord account you're trying to redeem this promotion on currently has a Nitro subscription so it is ineligible for this Nitro promotion.

Please make sure you're logged into the account that you want to redeem this promotion on. Or you can give the promotion link to a friend who hasn't had Nitro before.

Q: I see a "Sorry, looks like you've already had a Nitro sub!" error when I try to redeem my Nitro promo link.

A: If you're seeing a "Sorry, looks like you've already had a Nitro sub" error, that means that you've previously subscribed to Nitro on your Discord account in the past 12 months and you won't be able to redeem this 1 month perk. However, this promo link can be gifted to a friend.

If you have never subscribed to Nitro, please submit a ticket through our support system: https://dis.gd/contact and our support team will be able to investigate further.

Be sure to include your full Discord ID and email address tied to your Discord account.

Q: I see a "This gift has already been redeemed" error when I try to redeem my Nitro promo link.

A: If you are seeing a "This gift has been redeemed already" error, that means that the Nitro promo link has already been used and cannot be used again. You may need to double check if you've redeemed this promo link on another Discord account.

In particular, if you redeemed this promo link using your mobile device, double check the browser on your mobile device and see which Discord account you are currently logged into.

Unfortunately, once the promo link has been redeemed, the promo link cannot be re-enabled, and the Nitro cannot be transferred from one account to another.

Q: I see a "Wait a Second...Looks like this code didn't work." error when I try to redeem my Nitro promo link.

A: If you're seeing a "Wait a Second...Looks like this code didn't work." error, that means that the promo link is invalid. If you've copy and pasted this link, we recommend you double check the link you were given once more and make sure it exactly matches the link sent to your email.

If you received this link from a friend, double check with your friend on the exact link to make sure that it matches the link in their email.

Please note that our support team is unable to intervene if you or a friend has been given an invalid promo link and we will not be able to provide a new promo link.

Q: I see a "Sorry, This Payment Source Cannot Be Used for Redemption" error when trying to redeem my promo link!

A: If you're seeing a "Sorry, This Payment Source Cannot Be Used for Redemption" error, that means that the payment method you've selected to cover the temporary $1 hold cannot be used for that purpose.

Please keep in mind that prepaid payment methods, such as Gcash, cannot be used to cover temporary holds due to the nature of how prepaid payment methods function.

For more information on temporary holds, please check out this article!

Q: I'm having trouble with my GOG purchase or GOG Galaxy account.

A: Reach out to GOG's support team: https://support.gog.com/hc/en-us

articles.name: How to Manage Your Discord Profile Badges
articles.title: How to Manage Your Discord Profile Badges
articles.body:
Profile badges are the small icons on your profile that show off what you've done on Discord, from boosting servers to completing Quests. This article explains where to find your badges, what badge rarity means, and how to choose which badges appear on your profile.

What this article covers:

  • The Badge Directory
    • How to Open the Badge Directory
  • Badge Rarity
  • Managing Your Badges
    • Display Slots
    • Hiding a Badge
    • Reordering Your Badges
  • Frequently Asked Questions
Want to learn more? 
To learn what each badge means, visit Discord Profile Badges: What Each Badge Means.

The Badge Directory

The Badge Directory is your home base for profile badges. It shows you everything in one place:

  • The badges you've already unlocked
  • The badges that are available to earn
  • How to earn each badge

You can also learn about badges you spot on other people's profiles. Hover a badge on someone's profile to see more about it. Select each to find out how to earn it yourself.

How to Open the Badge Directory

Option 1: From a desktop or mobile profile

1. Open your profile or someone else's profile.

2. Select any badge (the icons next to the username) to open the Badge Directory.

If you're on your own Edit Profile screen, selecting a badge opens the Badge Customization panel instead. From there, select View Badges to go to the Badge Directory.

Option 2: From the desktop account popout

1. Select the You Bar at the bottom of the left sidebar.

2. Select Badges to open the Badge Directory.

Option 3: From the mobile You Bar

1. Tap the You Bar at the bottom of the app.

2. Tap the row of badges below your username to open the Badge Directory.

Important: Badge Directory on mobile is currently an experiment and is only available to a small number of mobile users at this time.

Badge Rarity

Every badge has a rarity: Common, Rare, Epic, or Mythic. Rarity shows how likely you are to come across other users with that badge on Discord. You'll see Common badges often, while Mythic badges are held by very few people.

Some badges evolve, which means they level up as you reach new milestones. Each level of an evolving badge can have its own rarity, so the same badge might be Common at its first level and Mythic at its highest.

Note: Badge rarity may change over time as more or fewer people earn a badge.
Tip: You can check any badge's rarity in the Badge Directory, or by selecting a badge on your profile or a friend's profile. While arranging your badges, you can also hover over a badge, open the menu, and select View Badge Details.

Managing Your Badges

Once you've earned a few badges, you can choose how they appear on your profile. Everyone can hide badges, and Nitro subscribers can also reorder them.

Note: Hiding and reordering badges is available on desktop, browser, and mobile.

Display Slots

Your profile displays up to six badges in its display slots. New badges that you earn and badges that you level up will be placed into your badge display slots by default. Additional badges that you've earned are kept in your Badge Directory, so visitors to your profile can still see everything you've unlocked.

Hiding a Badge

You can hide eligible badges you've earned so they don't appear on your profile.

Note: If you're a Nitro subscriber, your Nitro badge always stays visible to help others understand your profile's Nitro perks. You can still reorder it and hide your other badges.

On Desktop and Browser

1. Select the You Bar at the bottom of the left sidebar. Then, navigate to Edit Profile.

2. Select your Badges in the profile editor.

3. Select Customize Your Badges.

4. Hover over the badge you want to hide and select the three-dot menu.

5. Select Hide Badge.

6. Select Save to confirm.

Hidden badges move to the end of the row and show a small hidden icon so you can find and unhide them later. Other users won't see hidden badges on your profile.

Tip: You can also open the Badge Customization panel from the You Bar. Select your avatar at the bottom of the left sidebar, then press Badges.

On Mobile

1. Tap the You Bar at the bottom of the app.

2. Tap Edit Profile.

3. Tap Badges to open the Badge Customization panel.

4. Long press the badge you want to hide.

5. Tap Hide Badge.

6. Tap Save to confirm.

The badge moves to the end of the row and shows a small hidden icon, so you can still find it in this view later.

Reordering Your Badges

Note: Reordering badges is only available to Nitro subscribers.

As a Nitro subscriber, you can rearrange your badges to choose which ones fill your six display slots.

On Desktop and Browser

1. Select the You Bar at the bottom of the left sidebar. Then, navigate to Edit Profile.

2. Select your Badges to open the Badge Customization panel.

3. Select and drag a Badge to a new spot.

Tip: You can also open the Badge Customization panel from the You Bar. Select your avatar at the bottom of the left sidebar, then press Badges.

On Mobile

1. Tap the You Bar at the bottom of the app.

2. Tap Edit Profile.

3. Tap Badges to open Customize your badges.

4. Press and hold a Badge, then drag it to a new spot.

5. Tap Save to confirm your changes.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Can I remove a badge from my account?

A: Badges can't be removed from your account, but you can hide any badge so it doesn't appear on your profile. See Hiding a Badge above.

Q: Can I move my badges to a different account?

A: No. Profile badges are non-transferable and stay with the account that earned them.

Q: What happens to my badge order if my Nitro subscription ends?

A: If your Nitro subscription ends, your custom badge order will no longer apply. Your badges will go back to the default order shown for users without Nitro.

Q: Why don't I see a badge I just earned in my display slots?

A: Newly earned badges automatically move to the front of your display slots, so they should appear on your profile right away. If you don't see a badge you expected, try restarting or refreshing your Discord app.

If it still doesn't appear, you may not have met all the requirements to earn it yet. Check Discord Profile Badges: What Each Badge Means for details on how to earn each badge.

Q: Can I hide my Nitro badge?

A: No, Nitro badges are always visible. Nitro badges let others know why your profile looks the way it does, from animated avatars to custom emojis in your status. You can still reorder your badges and hide other badges.

Q: Will Discord add new badges?

A: New badges may be added over time. When they are, you'll find them in your Badge Directory.

To learn what each badge means, visit Discord Profile Badges: What Each Badge Means.

Want to learn more? 
Discord Profile Badges: What Each Badge Means

articles.name: Discord Profile Badges: What Each Badge Means
articles.title: Discord Profile Badges: What Each Badge Means
articles.body:
Learn what each Discord profile badge means and how it's unlocked, from the Discord Nitro badge to legacy badges that are no longer available.

Want to learn more? To learn how to open your Badge Directory, check badge rarity, and hide or reorder your badges, visit How to Manage Your Discord Profile Badges.

What this article covers:

  • Current Badges
    • Account Age Badge
    • Game Time Badge
    • Game Variety Badge
    • Gifting Badge
    • Nitro Badge
    • Orbs Badge
    • Quests Badge
    • Server Booster Badge
    • Streaming Badge
  • Legacy Badges
    • Early Supporter Badge
    • HypeSquad Events Badge
    • HypeSquad House Badges
    • Last Meadow Online Badge
    • Legacy Username Badge
    • Moderator Program Alumni Badge
    • Partnered Server Owner Badge
  • Other Badges You Might See
    • Bug Hunter Badge
    • Discord Staff Badge
  • Frequently Asked Questions

Current Badges

These badges can currently be unlocked. Details for each one are also available in your Badge Directory.

Account Age Badge

The Account Age badge reflects how long your account has existed. It unlocks once your account is a year old and evolves as your account gets older. Once you unlock a level, you won't lose it or drop back to a lower level. The badge evolves as time goes on.

Game Time Badge

The Game Time badge reflects the total time you've spent playing games that Discord can detect. Time across all detected games counts toward the same total, and the badge evolves as that total grows. Unfortunately, games you play on consoles, like Xbox or PlayStation, don't count toward the Game Time badge, since only the Discord desktop app can detect games. Game Time includes time played on or after December 8, 2025. Badge progress may take some time to reflect your recent activity.

To count progress toward these badges, turn on Use data to personalize my Discord experience. Check Data Used to Personalize Discord for details on how to enable this setting.

Game Variety Badge

The Game Variety badge reflects how many different games you've played that Discord recognizes. The badge evolves as that number grows.

Discord recognizes most desktop games automatically, though some very small games may not be detected. Some platforms are tracked as a single game. For example, playing different experiences in Roblox or Fortnite counts as one game.

Games you play on consoles, like Xbox or PlayStation, don't count toward the Game Variety badge. This badge only tracks games detected by the Discord desktop app. Badge progress may take some time to reflect your recent activity.

To count progress toward these badges, turn on Use data to personalize my Discord experience. Check Data Used to Personalize Discord for details on how to enable this setting.

Gifting Badge

The Gifting badge reflects the gifts you've sent on Discord. Every gift you've sent counts toward this badge, and it evolves as you send more Nitro or Shop gifts.

Nitro Badge

If you see this badge on an account, it means that they're subscribed to Nitro! Anyone subscribed to Nitro, Nitro Classic, or Nitro Basic has the Discord Nitro badge on their profile.

This badge evolves the longer you stay subscribed. Hover over the badge to see the subscription date and how long someone has been subscribed.

Learn more about everything included with a subscription in our Nitro FAQ.

Orbs Badge

You can purchase the Orbs badge from the Orbs shop to display on your profile. For more information about Discord Orbs and how they work, visit our Discord Orbs FAQ.

Quests Badge

The Discord Quests badge is for those who have completed a Quest! Quests let you discover games, earn rewards, and stream gameplay to friends. When you complete a Quest, the Discord Quests badge is added to your profile. For more information, visit our Discord Quests FAQ.

Server Boosting Badge

This pink badge represents a user who directly supports one of their favorite servers through Server Boosting. Hover over the Server Boosting badge to see how long someone has been boosting.

This badge evolves based on how long you've been boosting without a pause.

Note: If you stop boosting, or you're no longer boosting any servers, your boosting streak and badge reset to the first level. If you boost multiple servers, your badge always reflects your longest Server Boost streak.

You can learn more about Server Boosting in our Server Boosting FAQ.

Streaming Badge

The Streaming badge reflects the time you've spent sharing your screen with others. Time counts whenever you're sharing your screen with at least one other person in the call.

This badge only tracks streaming done on the Discord desktop app. The Streaming badge includes screen sharing on or after January 1, 2024. Badge progress may take some time to reflect your recent activity.

To count progress toward these badges, turn on Use data to personalize my Discord experience. Check Data Used to Personalize Discord for details on how to enable this setting.

Legacy Badges

Legacy badges can no longer be unlocked, but if you already earned one, it stays with your account. These badges reflect programs and events from Discord's earlier days.

Early Supporter Badge

Before there were two styles of Discord Nitro, there was a legacy version of Nitro Classic. After expanding our Nitro offerings, we granted the Early Supporter badge to anyone who supported us in the early years of Discord as a thank you gift!

Anyone who purchased Nitro at any point before Wednesday, October 10th, 2018 received this badge. Learn more about this badge in our Legacy Nitro Classic FAQ.

HypeSquad Events Badge

Along with the HypeSquad House badges, there was also a HypeSquad Events badge. Users earned this badge by attending an event in the name of HypeSquad. Event Coordinators ran the events themselves, such as organizing a university club or planning a LAN event.

HypeSquad House Badges

In the past, you could earn a HypeSquad House badge by taking a quiz in Discord that sorted you into one of three houses. The quiz is no longer available.

Last Meadow Online Badge

From April 1, 2026 to April 7, 2026, you could play Last Meadow Online to earn the Last Meadow Online badge. Hovering over the badge displays your level progression in the game. Learn more about the game in our Last Meadow Online announcement.

Legacy Username Badge

The Legacy Username badge lets other users know that you've kept your old username and discriminator. Learn more in our New Usernames and Display Names article.

Moderator Program Alumni Badge

Long ago, we granted the Certified Discord Moderator badge to those who were part of our moderation programs. These users received the badge to show they'd mastered the Moderator Academy courses and were active participants in our moderator program ecosystem.

The badge has since evolved into the Moderator Program Alumni badge, as a way to thank everyone who was part of our moderator ecosystem before Thursday, December 1st, 2022. To learn more about moderating on Discord, check out our Safety Center's Moderation page.

Partnered Server Owner Badge

Designed for active and engaged communities, the Partner Program distinguished the best servers out there. The Partnered Server Owner badge was given to owners of thriving communities and creators who showed an authentic enthusiasm for Discord.

Other Badges You Might See

Bug Hunter Badge

A mastermind of QA testing and detective work, the Bug Hunter badge is awarded to the most hard-working members of the Bug Hunter community. There's even a Golden Bug Hunter badge for those who reach the highest hunter level by going above and beyond!

A: No. These badges can only be unlocked and leveled up using the Discord desktop app.

Q: Why isn't my badge progress updating?

A: Badge progress may take some time to reflect your recent activity. If your progress still does not update, confirm that you are using the Discord desktop app and that the Use data to personalize my Discord experience setting is enabled. For instructions on enabling this setting, see Data Used to Personalize Discord.

Once you earn a badge, it appears in your Badge Directory along with details about how it was earned. To learn how to hide or reorder the badges on your profile, see How to Manage Your Discord Profile Badges.

articles.name: Discoverable Content on the Web
articles.title: Discoverable Content on the Web
articles.body:
Messages from public channels in Discoverable Servers can appear on the web through a server’s web pages, either as individual messages or as summaries of a channel's conversation. This article explains what that means for you as a member and how you can control your own content.

What this article covers:

  • What Content Can Appear on the Web
  • How will I know if I'm in a channel where this applies?
  • Controlling Whether Your Messages Can Appear
    • How to Turn This Setting On or Off
    • What Happens When You Change This Setting
    • Deleting Individual Messages
  • Can my messages appear on the web by default?
  • Frequently Asked Questions

What Content Can Appear on the Web

A Server Web Page can show two different kinds of content pulled from public channels:

  • Channel Summaries on the web: A small slice of what's being talked about in your server, directly on your Server Web Page. These automated summaries only cover discussions from November 16, 2026 onward. Admins can change which channels they draw from, curate the summaries that are shown, or turn them off entirely. Usernames will not be shown in summaries.
  • Channel Messages on the web: From mid-December 2026, answers to questions your members sent in public channels can be found in a web search, in their own words. Server admins decide which channels take part, and server members can choose whether their own messages appear. Usernames and avatars will not be shown alongside these messages.

How will I know if I'm in a channel where this applies?

Discoverable content on the web can only appear from public channels in a Discoverable Server. Channels taking part in Channel Summaries or Channel Messages are labeled, with an icon in the channel header, so you know before you send a message. 

You'll also see a pop-up near the channel header letting you know before you post. This pop-up reappears any time a channel newly enables this feature. Your server's admins choose which channels take part in Channel Summaries and Channel Messages on the web, so you may see this in some channels and not others.

Channel Messages roll out gradually from mid-December 2026, so it may be a few weeks before messages from labeled channels appear on Server Web Pages.

Controlling Whether Your Messages Can Appear

The Show my message content from Discoverable channels on web pages setting controls whether your messages in eligible channels can be shown on the public web. It applies across all your servers, not per server.

Note: You can change this setting on desktop or in your browser. It applies to your whole account, including on mobile.

How to Turn This Setting On or Off

1. Open User Settings.

2. Select Data & Privacy.

3. Turn Show my message content from Discoverable channels on web pages on or off.

Data & Privacy Setting for Web Pages

What Happens When You Change This Setting

Whether a message can appear on the web depends on your Channel Messages setting when you send it. Messages you send while the setting is off won't appear on the web.

Turning the setting off doesn't change this for messages you sent while it was on. Those messages can still appear on the server’s web pages, even if they haven't appeared yet. To prevent one of those messages from appearing, or to remove one that's already on Discord's web pages, delete it from Discord.

  • While your setting is on: eligible messages you send can appear publicly. Messages may be displayed by search engines (including, but not limited to Google), which may be based outside your country.
  • When you turn it off: Discord stops displaying on web any new messages from you going forward.
  • Messages already shown on web before you turned it off can remain visible. Turning the setting off is not a bulk "remove my history" action.

Deleting Individual Messages

If you delete an individual message, that deletion applies on Discord and is reflected on the Server Web Page, so the message will be removed there too. Deleting a message removes its visibility on the Discord app and Discord web pages. While Discord has its own data retention policy, we do not control how long others may retain cached or indexed copies of content. Search engines have their own deletion processes and retention policies so it may take additional action or time for content to stop appearing in their results.

Can my messages appear on the web by default?

Yes, in most regions. Your Channel Messages setting is on by default, so messages you send in Discoverable channels can appear on the web unless you turn it off. It's off by default if your account is in the EU/EEA, UK, Canada, Brazil, Australia, or South Korea. If you're in the teen age group, your messages won't appear on the web and you can't turn this setting on.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Can I stop my messages from appearing on the web as Channel Messages?

A: Yes. Turn off your Channel Messages setting in User Settings > Data & Privacy (Show my message content from Discoverable channels on web pages). This applies to messages you send from then on. Messages you sent while the setting was on can still appear on the web.

Q: If I delete a message, does it disappear from search results?

A: Deleting a message removes it from Discord and from Discord’s web pages. Search engines keep their own copies of pages, so it may take some time, or an extra removal request, before it stops appearing in their results. Discord doesn’t control how long they keep cached copies. Learn more about how long Discord keeps your information in our data retention policy.

Q: What happens if I don't change anything?

A: If you do nothing, eligible messages you send starting mid-December 2026 may appear on the web, unless your region or account defaults it off (default off in EU/EEA, UK, Canada, Brazil, Australia, or South Korea).

It may be a few weeks before messages from labeled channels appear on a server’s web pages. Channel Messages on the web must also meet server, channel, and content requirements.

Q: Are messages in threads and forums included?

A: Yes, if the parent channel is public, eligible, and Channel Summaries on web or Channel Messages on web is turned on for the channel. Private threads and private forums are never included, regardless of the parent channel’s settings.

Q: Are messages text only?

A: Currently, Channel Messages on the web will show text only. A small number of existing partner communities have images and videos appearing on their Server Web Pages today as part of an earlier pilot. We’ll update this answer as that capability becomes more broadly available.

Q: Are you selling my messages to AI companies?

A: No. Nothing has changed. We are making Discord content easier to find if admins and users choose to make their content available on the web.

articles.name: Discoverable Server Web Presence
articles.title: Discoverable Server Web Presence
articles.body:
Web Presence is where you control what content from your Discoverable Server can appear publicly on its Server Web Page and in search engines like Google.

Note: Web Presence settings are available on desktop and browser only at this time. Only the server owner or members with the Administrator permission can change them, and bots can't change them.

Want to learn more? 
Learn more about Server Web Pages. To learn how members control their own messages, see Discoverable Content on Web.

What this article covers:

  • How to Open Web Presence
  • What You Can Control Here
    • What makes a channel eligible?
    • Channel Summaries on the Web
    • Channel Messages on the Web
    • Setting This When Creating a Channel
  • Removing Content from the Web
  • Frequently Asked Questions

How to Open Web Presence

1. Open Server Settings.

2. Under Community, select Web Presence.

Web Presence in Server Settings

Tip: The first time you visit your server on desktop after October 27, 2026, you may see a pop-up titled Reach new members on the web. Select Web Presence to go straight to these settings.

Reach new members on the web Pop-up

What You Can Control Here

Controls for both Channel Summaries on the web and Channel Messages on the web roll out gradually starting October 27, 2026.

Server Web Presence manages two independent features. Each has its own toggle and its own list of eligible channels. Both toggles are under Discoverable Content on Web Pages and are on by default.

  • Channel Summaries on the web: These show a small slice of what's being talked about in your server, directly on your Server Web Page. These automated summaries focus on active conversations from November 16, 2026, onwards. Admins can change which channels they draw from, curate the summaries that are shown, or turn them off entirely. Usernames and avatars will not be shown in summaries.

Channel Summaries Channel Settings

  • Channel Messages on the web: From mid-December 2026, answers to questions your members sent in public channels can be found in a web search, in their own words. Server admins decide which channels take part, and server members can choose whether their own messages appear. Usernames and avatars will not be shown alongside these messages.

Channel Messages Settings

What makes a channel eligible?

From November 16, 2026, summaries from public channels in your Discoverable Server may appear on your Server Web Page. Starting mid-December 2026, messages from public channels can appear too. Private channels, like role-restricted channels, are never included.

Channels taking part in Channel Summaries or Channel Messages are labeled, with an icon in the channel header.

Public channels in Discoverable Servers are included by default. You can change which ones are included at any time. Read below for more information on toggles for Channel Summaries on the web and Channel Messages on the web.

Channel Summaries on the Web

Choose which channels contribute to Channel Summaries on your Server Web Page. You can:

  • Select or deselect individual channels
  • Turn Summaries off entirely for your server

Use Search channels to find a specific channel, or select Select All or Deselect All to change every channel at once. Select Save Changes when you're done.

Summaries are generated automatically and are subject to Discord's Discovery Guidelines. Discord's Trust & Safety team can remove summaries that violate these guidelines.

Channel Messages on the Web

Choose which channels are eligible to have members' messages shown on the server web pages. You can:

  • Select or deselect individual channels, independently of your Channel Summaries selections
  • Turn Channel Messages off entirely for your server

Setting This When Creating a Channel

When you create a public text channel in a Discoverable Server, the channel creation window includes a Discoverable section where you can choose All Content, Summaries Only, Messages Only, or Off. This only changes the channel you're creating. For private channels, this section shows as Disabled.

Removing Content from the Web

To remove a Channel Summary or Channel Message from your Server Web Page:

  • Delete the message. Deleting a message removes it from the Discord app and Discord web pages.
  • Turn off the feature. Toggling off Channel Summaries or Channel Messages stops new content from being generated or shown going forward, but content already published may remain visible until individually removed.
  • Remove specific channels. Deselect individual channels under Web Presence settings to stop them from contributing new content.

Keep in mind that while Discord removes content from its own pages, search engines have their own caching and indexing processes. It may take additional time or action for content to stop appearing in search results.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: How do I know if my server is Discoverable?

A: Open Server Settings > Access > Discoverable. If your server meets all requirements and Server Discovery is turned on, your server is Discoverable, and the settings in this article apply to it. If you can't open the Discoverable tab, or your server doesn't meet all Server Discovery requirements, it isn't Discoverable yet. See What if my server doesn't meet requirements? above, or learn how a server becomes Discoverable in Clarifying Server Types. 

Q: What happens if I don't do anything?

A: If you don't do anything, starting November 16, 2026, Channel Summaries may start appearing on your Server Web Page, and Channel Messages will roll out starting mid-December 2026. If you haven't published your own Server Web Page, a default page goes live for you on November 16, 2026.

In some regions, members' Channel Messages setting is off by default, so their messages won't appear unless they turn it on.

If you want to turn off or change these settings, visit Server Settings > Community > Web Presence.

Q: If I turn off Channel Summaries or Channel Messages, does existing content come down immediately?

A: Turning off a feature stops new content from being generated or shown going forward. Content already published may remain visible until it's individually removed. Deleting a message removes its visibility on the Discord app and Discord web pages. While Discord has its own data retention policy, we do not control how long others may retain cached or indexed copies of content. Search engines have their own deletion processes and retention policies so it may take additional action or time for content to stop appearing in their results.

Q: Can I stop my server from appearing on the web entirely?

A: Turning off both Channel Summaries and Channel Messages stops new content from appearing, though content already published may remain visible (see the FAQ above). Your Server Web Page stays live while your server is Discoverable. To remove your Server Web Page, turn off Discoverability, which changes your server back to a Community Server. See Clarifying Server Types for how to do this.

Q: Do Channel Summaries and Channel Messages use the same channel selections?

A: No. They're independent. You can select different channels for each, or turn one off without affecting the other.

Q: How are Channel Summaries created?

A: Discord creates Channel Summaries using AI, based on recent discussions in your server's public channels. Summaries may not always be accurate.

Q: Is Discord selling user messages to AI companies?

A: No. Nothing has changed. We are making Discord content easier to find if admins and users choose to make their content available on the web.

Q: What happens if my server stops being Discoverable?

A: If your server is no longer Discoverable, your Server Web Page is taken down, and Channel Messages and Channel Summaries turn off so your server no longer contributes new content to these features. However, this does not automatically remove content that was already published on the web.

To remove a specific message from Discord web pages, delete the original message in Discord. Search engines may still have cached copies, even after the message is deleted. Discord doesn't control those copies, so removal from search results may require additional time or action through the search engine.

See Clarifying Server Types for more about what changes when you turn off Discoverability.

Q: Does turning off a feature here affect my members' individual privacy settings?

A: No. Members have their own separate control over whether their individual messages can appear. Members control this with the Show my message content from Discoverable channels on web pages setting in User Settings > Data & Privacy.

Region, age, and each member's own privacy setting can affect whether a specific message is eligible. See Discoverable Content on Web to learn more about individual user controls.

articles.name: What is Decree No. 12,976/2026
articles.title: What is Decree No. 12,976/2026
articles.body:
Note: Individuals to whom Decree 12,976/2026 does not apply may submit reports of non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII) through our standard in-app reporting system. Our non-consensual intimate imagery policy applies globally in addition to other legal rights you may have where you live.

Decree No. 12,976/2026 is a Brazilian federal regulation issued under Brazil's Marco Civil da Internet that sets out guidelines for protecting women online and addressing violence against women in digital environments. It requires covered platforms like Discord to: 

  • provide a clear reporting channel;
  • review removal requests, including notifications about crimes or unlawful acts or coordinated harassment committed against women because of their gender;
  • remove non-consensual intimate content within a defined timeframe; 
  • take reasonable steps to limit the spread of that content; and 
  • block artificial intelligence (AI) tools from generating or altering intimate images of real people without their consent. 
Important: Need immediate help? If you have concerns about your personal safety, or the safety of someone you know, please contact local law enforcement or social services.

What this article covers:

  • Your Rights and Our Responsibilities Under Decree No. 12,976/2026
  • What to Expect After You Submit a Removal Request Under Decree No. 12,976/2026

Your Rights and Our Responsibilities Under Decree No. 12,976/2026

If Decree No. 12,976/2026 applies to you, you or a representative acting on your behalf may:

  • Submit a request for Discord to remove the content that was shared without your consent. That includes images, video, audio, text, or any combination of these that depicts nudity, partial nudity, a sexual act, or a sexualized context, including content wholly or partly generated or manipulated by AI.
  • Learn more on how to report this content to Discord for removal via our dedicated reporting channel.  

If you're outside Brazil, or you're reporting images of someone else that you don’t have legal authority to represent, you can report content under our Non-Consensual Intimate Imagery policy via our standard reporting process using the in-app report menu.

Important: Please note that intimate imagery of a person under the age of 18 constitutes Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM). We report illegal child sexual abuse material and grooming to the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC). Discord takes enforcement action against users who post such content.

Discord’s obligations as a covered provider under Decree 12,976/2026 include:

  • Maintain a permanent, free, and easily accessible space for receiving reports of non-consensual intimate content and other forms of gender-based violence, with confirmation of receipt and a way for the reporting party to track their case;
  • Display information about Brazil's Women’s Assistance Center (Call 180) helpline;
  • Take swift action when Discord receives a valid report, making reasonable efforts to identify and remove known copies of the same visual depiction, and applying measures to help block re-uploads of the same content;
  • Take steps to reduce the reach and visibility of coordinated attacks or harassment against women.

What to Expect After You Submit a Removal Request Under Decree No. 12,976/2026

We will confirm receipt of your report and review it to determine whether the reported content falls within the scope of the Decree.

  • We will promptly review your request to confirm that it meets the requirements of the Decree. 
  • If your report concerns non-consensual intimate content, and the request is valid and complete, we will remove the reported content and we will make reasonable efforts to identify and remove known copies to prevent it from being re-uploaded.
  • If your report concerns another form of gender-based violence covered by the Decree, we will evaluate it and communicate our decision — including the reasoning — to you and, where relevant, to the user who posted the content. We will not share the information in your report with users who posted the content to Discord. They will only be notified that the content has been removed, not who reported it.

If your submission is incomplete, we may be unable to process it until you provide the missing information.

articles.name: Non-Consensual Intimate Imagery Reporting Under the UK Online Safety Act (OSA)
articles.title: Non-Consensual Intimate Imagery Reporting Under the UK Online Safety Act (OSA)
articles.body:
Note: Individuals to whom the UK Online Safety Act does not apply may submit reports of non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII) through our standard in-app reporting system. Our non-consensual intimate imagery policy applies globally in addition to other legal rights you may have where you live.

The Online Safety Act (OSA) is a UK law that applies to companies like Discord and carries certain obligations regarding illegal content, including non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII), sometimes referred to as "revenge porn" or "image-based sexual abuse." Under the OSA and relevant codes of practice, covered platforms, like Discord, must provide a clear reporting process, review qualifying removal requests, remove NCII content, and use tools such as hash-matching to help prevent that content from being shared or re-uploaded.

Important: Need immediate help? If you have concerns about your personal safety, or the safety of someone you know, please contact local law enforcement or social services.

What this article covers:

  • Our Responsibilities Under the OSA
  • What to Expect After You Submit a Removal Request Under the OSA

Our Responsibilities Under the OSA

If you are affected, you, or a representative acting on your behalf, may:

  • Notify Discord of any non-consensual intimate image published on Discord that depicts you and was shared without your consent; and,
  • Submit a request for Discord to remove the content. For more details about how to submit a removal request, you can refer to our help article.

So that we can help you, please make sure your removal request meets these requirements:

  • You are identifiable in the content or via the context in which it is displayed (for example, your face is visible or your name is mentioned);
  • The content shows you nude, partially nude, or engaged in sexual activity; and,
  • The content was shared without your consent.

Discord may also action content submitted for removal through this process even if it does not meet the criteria above, such as for violation of our Community Guidelines, or where other UK laws may apply. Discord also reports content that it reasonably believes depicts persons under the age of 18 years old to the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children, and takes enforcement action against users who post such content. 

Under the OSA, Discord, as a regulated service, is required to:

  • Maintain a clear and accessible process that allows an affected individual (or their authorised representative) to report non-consensual intimate imagery;
  • Review each report and assess it against illegal content requirements;
  • Remove the reported content confirmed to be illegal NCII within the 48 hour time period required by law; and,
  • Make reasonable efforts to identify and remove known copies of the same non-consensual intimate visual depiction.

What to Expect After You Submit a Removal Request Under the OSA

We will promptly review your report to assess whether the content meets the legal requirements for removal. If your report is complete and the content is confirmed to be non-consensual intimate imagery, we will remove it and take reasonable steps to prevent known copies from being re-shared, including through hash-matching where applicable.

If your submission is incomplete, we may be unable to process your report until sufficient information is provided.

You can also find independent support from organisations such as the Revenge Porn Helpline or StopNCII.org.

articles.name: Get a Riot Cash Code When You Subscribe to Nitro
articles.title: Get a Riot Cash Code When You Subscribe to Nitro
articles.body:
Discord has partnered with Riot Games to offer eligible new Nitro subscribers a Riot Cash Code, redeemable for in-game currency in select Riot Games titles.

What this article covers:

  • What is a Riot Cash Code?
  • Eligibility Requirements
  • How to Get Your Riot Cash Code
  • How to Access Your Code
  • Frequently Asked Questions
Offer: This offer is available to certain new Nitro subscribers who subscribe September 30 and October 14, 2026 at 12pm ET. Refer to our Eligibility Requirements below for more details. Current Nitro subscribers aren't eligible. You must claim your code by October 28, 2026.

What is a Riot Cash Code?

A Riot Cash Code is a $10 code redeemable for in-game currency in select Riot Games titles, including League of Legends and VALORANT. When you subscribe to Nitro for the first time, you can unlock a Riot Cash Code as a welcome incentive.

Eligibility Requirements

You are eligible if:

  • You subscribe to Nitro (not Nitro Basic) as a new subscriber. Subscribing unlocks your Riot Cash Code. 
  • You have an active League of Legends and/or VALORANT account that you've played on within the last 180 days.
  • You are located in the United States.

You are not eligible if:

  • You already have an active Discord Nitro subscription at the time of this offer.
  • You have Nitro Basic, Nitro Classic, or are currently using Nitro credits.
  • You have already received a Riot Cash Code through this offer. 
  • You have not played League of Legends or Valorant in the last 6 months

How to Get Your Riot Cash Code

  1. Subscribe to Nitro between September 30 and October 14, 2026 at 12pm ET.
  2. Once subscribed, your Riot Cash Code becomes available to claim in Nitro Home.

How to Access Your Code

1. On desktop or browser, select Nitro Home in the left sidebar.

Nitro Home Tab on Desktop

2. Under Nitro Rewards, locate the Redeem a $10 Riot Games reward card.

Redeem a $10 Riot Games reward Card on Desktop

3. Select Unlock Reward.

4. Copy your code, or select Redeem Code to use it right away.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Do I need a Nitro subscription to get a Riot Cash Code?

A: Yes. This offer is available to certain new Nitro subscribers. Refer to our Eligibility Requirements above for more details. 

Q: I already have an active Nitro subscription. Can I still get a Riot Cash Code?

A: No, this offer is available to new subscribers only. If you're already subscribed to Nitro, you're not eligible for this offer.

Q: Where do I redeem my Riot Cash Code?

A: You can redeem your code at shop.riotgames.com while logged into your Riot Games account, or through the prepaid codes and cards section at checkout in participating Riot titles.

Q: What if codes for this offer run out?

A: Codes are limited. If none are available when you check, you'll see a message letting you know more are on the way, and you can check back later.

Q: Does my Riot Cash Code expire?

A: Your code doesn't expire once you've claimed it, but you must claim it in Nitro Home by October 28, 2026. If you don't claim it by then, you won't be able to get your code.

Q: I think I found a bug. How do I report it?

A: If you're experiencing technical issues or suspect you've encountered a bug, please reach out to Discord Support for help. We can investigate and assist you further.

Want to learn more?

Learn more about Nitro subscription benefits.

Redemption

Q: Can I redeem my Nameplate on mobile?

Q. Why don't I see my free Nameplate?

Q: Who can claim this promotion from their T-Life app?

Q: Who can redeem this Nitro trial to their Discord account?

If your Discord transaction history does not show the hold released after 5 business days, please let us know at https://dis.gd/contact, and our support team will be able to investigate this issue further.

It looks like you have Nitro already" error, that means that the Discord account you're trying to redeem this promotion on currently has a Nitro membership so it is ineligible for this Nitro promotion. Please make sure you're logged into the account that you want to redeem this promotion on.

Q: I see a "This gift has already been claimed" error when I try to claim my Nitro promo.

Q: I see a "Looks like something went wrong" error when I click on "Next".

Please note that the support team is unable to assist you if you run into this error and we are not able to increase the limit of claims.

Q: I see a "Looks like your email isn't verified. Make sure to verify your email before claiming this gift."

A: If you are seeing a "Looks like your email isn't verified, make sure to verify your email before claiming this gift" error, you are trying to redeem this Nitro promotion on a Discord account with an email that hasn't been verified yet. Desktop/Browser

articles.name: Custom Typing Indicator FAQ
articles.title: Custom Typing Indicator FAQ
articles.body:
Customize the “is typing…” message that appears when you're the only one typing, with your own emoji and status word.

What this article covers:

  • Custom Typing Indicator: What Is It?
  • How to Customize Your Typing Indicator
    • Settings
    • Profile
  • Nitro vs. Non-Nitro Access
  • Frequently Asked Questions
Important: This is currently an experiment in beta and isn't widely available yet. Only a limited number of Nitro subscribers can access it right now, and it's only available on mobile.

Custom Typing Indicator: What Is It?

“Is typing…” is the default message you see when someone's composing a message. With Custom Typing Indicator, you can replace that default message with your own 3 emojis and status word whenever you're the only person typing. 

Note: If more than one person is typing at the same time, everyone's indicator returns to the default “is typing…” message.

Currently available on mobile only, this appears anywhere you can chat on Discord, including direct messages, text channels, forum channels, and voice channel chats.

There are three parts you can customize:

  • Emoji: Select 3 unique emoji that you already have access to.
  • Animation: Choose an animation style: Pulse, Ring, or Wave, or select None to turn animation off.
  • Status: Pick a status word from a preset list to replace "typing," like "is yapping…" or "is daydreaming…"

Example of a Customized Typing Indicator

How to Customize Your Typing Indicator

Note: This feature is currently mobile only as part of the experiment in beta. During this experiment, you'll be able to set up your custom typing indicator from one of two places: Settings or your Profile, not both. We're experimenting in two places, so you'll only see one.

Settings

1. Tap the You Bar and select Settings.

2. Scroll to App Settings and tap Typing Indicator. 

Navigating from Settings to Typing Indicator

3. Select an emoji slot to open the emoji picker. Selecting your first emoji fills all 3 emoji slots at once, so you always start with a complete set. You can then select each slot again to swap in different emoji.

4. Select Animation to open the motion sheet and choose a style (screen name and options not yet locked).

5. Select Text to open the status word list and choose from our options of preset status words to replace “typing”.

6. Once you've made a change, select Apply to save your customized typing indicator. 

Customizing Your Typing Indicator in Settings

Note: Some long usernames or status words display as much as they can on a single line, then get cut off with an ellipsis depending on your screen size. For example: "mallowmallowmallowmallow is bab…"

Tip: Can't decide on a combo? Select Surprise Me and let Discord mix up your emoji, animation, and status word for you. It's a great way to discover a combo you wouldn't have picked yourself! Not feeling the result? Tap Reset to clear your selections and start over.

Customizing Your Typing Indicator Using Surprise Me and Reset

Profile

1. Tap the You Bar and select Edit Profile.

2. Tap Typing Indicator. 

Navigating from Your Profile to Typing Indicator

3. Select your emoji, animation, and text, then Apply to save your customized typing indicator.

Customizing Your Typing Indicator from your Profile

Note: If a server has the Use External Emoji permission turned off, other members in that server will see the default "…" in place of your custom emoji, but they'll still see your custom status word (for example, "is yapping…").

Tip: Tapping on someone else's Custom Typing Indicator opens the same bottom sheet you'd use to set up your own. It can be used as a quick shortcut to jump straight into customizing yours by tapping Check it Out. 
This only works if you're able to edit your typing indicator; some users can only view others' custom indicators at this time. 

 

In-app Sheet for Custom Typing Indicator

Nitro vs. Non-Nitro Access

  • Nitro members: Can fully customize and save their typing indicator, including emoji, animation, and status word. This feature is not available for Nitro Basic.
  • Non-Nitro members: Can preview the customization options but need a Nitro subscription to save and use them.

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: What does Custom Typing Indicator do?

A: It lets you replace the default “is typing…” message with up to 3 custom emoji, a motion style, and an alternative verb, whenever you're the only person typing in a conversation.

Q: Can I turn off the custom typing indicator?

A: There isn't a way to disable the custom typing indicator. If you'd like to reduce the intensity of its animation, you can turn on Reduced Motion in User Settings > Accessibility, which minimizes motion effects across Discord.

Q: What happens if more than one person is typing at the same time?

A: Everyone's typing indicator returns to the default “is typing…” message until only one person is typing again.

Q: Do I need Nitro to use this feature?

A: You need a Nitro subscription to save and use a custom typing indicator. This feature is not available for Nitro Basic. Non-Nitro members can preview the customization options, but can't save or apply them.

Q: Where can I set up my custom typing indicator?

A: As part of this experiment, you'll be able to set it up from either Settings or your Profile, but you'll only see one of the two. This experiment is currently mobile only.

Q: Will everyone see my custom typing indicator the same way?

A: Not always. If a server has the Use External Emoji permission turned off, other members in that server will see the default "…" in place of your custom emoji, but they'll still see your custom status word.

Q: Where does my custom typing indicator show up?

A: It shows up for others anytime you are typing on Discord, including direct messages, text channels, forum channels, and voice channel chats. It only appears if you are the only person typing. 

Q: Is this feature available to everyone?

A: Not yet. This is currently an experiment and only available to a limited number of Nitro subscribers on mobile. 

Q: Can I choose any word for my status?

A: You'll choose from a preset list of status words rather than writing your own. The current options are: is yapping…, is venting…, is oversharing…, is barking…, is babbling…, is daydreaming…, and is meowing….

Q: Is there a quick way to try different combinations?

A: Yes. Select Surprise Me to get a random combination of emoji, animation, and status word.

Q: Can I set a different typing indicator for each server?

A: No. Your custom typing indicator applies everywhere you chat on Discord and can't be set on a per-server basis.

Q: What happens if I tap on someone else's custom typing indicator?

A: If you're able to edit your own typing indicator, tapping on someone else's opens the same bottom sheet used to customize yours, so you can quickly set one up for yourself. If you can't edit your typing indicator, tapping won't open this shortcut.

articles.name: How Discord Confirms Your Age Group in Texas
articles.title: How Discord Confirms Your Age Group in Texas
articles.body:
Texas’s App Store Accountability Act requires apps like Discord to use age signals shared from the Apple App Store or Google Play Store to confirm your age group. In compliance with this law, Discord will receive your age range associated with your device’s app store. 

What this article covers:

  • How the App Store Age Check Works in Texas
  • What Happens If the Age Check Doesn’t Return a Result
  • Parental Controls and Account Access
  • Frequently Asked Questions

How the App Store Age Check Works in Texas

For Texas users, Discord receives the age range associated with your device’s app store automatically when you open the app. This is different from how age assurance on Discord works in most other regions, where you’re only prompted to confirm your age if you try to access age-restricted content, spaces, or settings. 
Here’s how the app store age range check works: 

  • Discord checks the account settings for your device’s app store account (such as your Apple or Google account) for an existing age range. You can refer to Apple or Google’s help pages for details on how to ensure your age is accurately reflected in your account.
  • If your app store account shows that you are 18 or older: you are placed in the adult age group and can access age-restricted content, spaces, and settings on Discord. 
  • If your app store account shows that you are between 13 and 17: you will be placed into the teen age group, and will not be able to access age-restricted content and spaces, or change certain settings (for example, you cannot disable Sensitive Content Filters). Messaging friends, joining voice calls, and accessing non age-restricted channels and servers all continue to work as normal. 

If your app store age range incorrectly shows that you’re a teen, you can refer to Apple or Google’s help pages for details on how to update the age that is associated with your account. You can also confirm your age through a different method, see How to Confirm Your Age Group on Discord for instructions. 

  • If your app store account shows that you are under 13: your account will be disabled because you must be at least 13 years old to use Discord.

What Happens If the Age Check Doesn’t Return a Result

If the check via the app store doesn’t return a result, you can continue using Discord as usual. You just won’t be able to access age-restricted content, spaces, or settings until you confirm you’re an adult, whether it’s through having your app store age range shared in the future, or through one of our other age assurance methods. 

Parental Controls and Account Access

Texas law also gives parents and guardians control over whether their teen can use apps like Discord at all, separate from the age assurance process. 

If your parent or guardian removes your permission to use Discord through your device’s app store parental controls, your account will be blocked from accessing Discord until your parent or guardian restores permission. There is no appeal process through Discord for this type of block, and access is restored only when your parent or guardian reverses the change in your device’s parental controls. If your account is blocked in this way; your servers, friends list, and message history will stay intact and will be restored if access is reinstated within our standard retention window of 2 years. Beyond that, your account will be subject to deletion like any other inactive Discord account. 

Note: If you're a parent or guardian, here’s how to restore access on Apple devices.

If you previously removed permissions for your teen to use Discord and want to allow it again:

1. Your teen will need to initiate an exception request. When trying to open an app with an age rating higher than the app age-rating restriction that you set for them, your teen will see a message that says content restrictions are enabled and can ask for an exception.

2. If they ask for an exception, you'll receive a message in Apple’s Messages app. You can approve or decline the request right from the message notification or in the Messages app.

3. On your device: When you tap Review the request, the app's page opens. You can approve or decline the exception, or view the app's Age Rating Details.

4. Discord will detect the restored permission and lift the account block automatically. No Discord support ticket or appeal is needed.

For more on how these age and consent rules work on Apple devices in Texas, see Apple's Age requirements for managing an Apple Account in Texas page.

Note: If you're a parent or guardian, here’s how to restore access on Android devices

If you previously removed permissions for your teen to use Discord and want to allow it again:

1. Open the Family Link app

2. Select your teen

3. Tap Screen time  > Time limits  > App limits

4. Select the Discord app

5. Tap App details  > Permissions

6. Switch the permission on

Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Do these changes apply to all Discord users in Texas? 

A: Yes, the automatic app store age range check applies to all new and existing Discord accounts in Texas when using Discord on their iOS or Android devices. 

Q: Why is my age range shared automatically, when users elsewhere are only asked to confirm their age when they try to access something age-restricted?

A: Texas's App Store Accountability Act requires app stores to share age signals automatically with developers like Discord, rather than checking when someone tries to access age-restricted content. That's why Texas users will have their age ranges shared automatically when opening Discord on an iOS or Android device. 

Q: What information does Discord receive from the app store check?

A: Discord only receives your age range (for example, whether you're 18 or older), not your name, Apple or Google ID, birthdate, or any other account information.

Q: What if I don't want to share my age from the app store?

A: Texas's App Store Accountability Act requires app stores to share age signals with developers like Discord for users in Texas, when opening Discord on an iOS or Android device. More details can be found in the Apple and Google help pages. 

Q: What happens if my app store account says I'm under 18 but I'm actually an adult?

A: If your app store age range is incorrect, you can refer to Apple or Google’s help pages for details on how to update the age that is associated with your account. You can also confirm your age through a different method, the same way any user can if they are initially placed in the wrong age group. See How to Confirm Your Age Group on Discord for instructions.

Q: If my age is shared through the app store once, will I need to confirm it again?

A: In most cases, no. However, if the age range from your app store account later changes (for example, if a parent or guardian updates or removes it), you may need to reconfirm your age. 

Q: Can a parent or guardian control my access to Discord separately from age assurance?

A: Yes, if a parent or guardian removes permission for you to use Discord through their app store parental controls you will be blocked from accessing Discord until they restore that permission. See Parental Controls and Account Access above.

Q: Can I appeal if I believe my account was incorrectly restricted?

A: If your app store age range that was shared is incorrect, you can refer to Apple or Google’s help pages for details on how to update the age that is associated with your account, or retry confirming your age. If your account was blocked because a parent or guardian removed app permissions (see Parental Controls and Account Access), those are separate permissions that can only be changed by your parent or guardian, not by retrying to confirm your age.

Q: If my Discord account was blocked via app store parental controls by my parent or guardian, can I unblock it once I turn 18?

A: Yes, assuming you turn 18 within our standard 2 year retention period for inactive accounts, you can end parental controls on your app store account. After, when you launch the Discord app your account will automatically unlock.
